text:
ben (PM): quick design check — exporting vectors from the batch preview. thinking through defaults: should export include full vector dims as columns, or a single base64/ndjson payload per row? thoughts? :file_folder:

sophia (Design): i prefer column-per-dim for quick csv analysis (spreadsheets). but header names need to be clear and not explode the UI. maybe a compact toggle: "CSV (flat)" vs "NDJSON (packed)" :eyes:

leo (Eng): column-per-dim is okay but we need to warn about file size — 1536 dims -> huge csv. backend can stream, but the client may OOM on download in-browser. we can implement streaming chunked responses and a server-side job for large exports.

ana: (typo) sorry meant ana (Accessibility): accessibility nits for the export modal: focus must land on the primary action, export format radio group needs aria-describedby for size estimates, and the download completion should fire an aria-live region update. also labels for the CSV column toggle should be explicit (e.g., "Include vector columns" not just "Flat").

ben (PM): good call. on defaults i was thinking: small batches: default flat csv with dims; large batches (>5k rows or >100k tokens) default to NDJSON and add a banner explaining why. we also need a sample-setting — let users export a random sample or top-k. eva, any research on what users typically do?

eva (Research): from interviews: data scientists often want a sample first, then full export. they like a seeded-sample option so results are reproducible. also dedupe option (remove near-duplicates) is requested when reranking outputs are noisy.

sophia (Design): copy suggestion for modal header: "Export vectors — choose format & sample". body line 1: "Export selected rows or full set. For large exports we'll create a background job and email/download link." buttons: "Start export" and secondary "Cancel". Add a small link: "Advanced options" -> exposes sample seed, dedupe threshold, include-metadata toggle.

leo (Eng): implementation notes: we can add a query param ?format=csv|ndjson&sample=%7Bsize,seed%7D&dedupe=0.8. For csv columns we'll emit header like: 
```
id,text,source,score,vector_0,vector_1,...,vector_511
```
If dims > 512 we name them vector_0...vector_N. We'll also gzip responses and support background export jobs with a signed download URL to avoid browser memory issues.

ana (Accessibility): small copy nits: avoid ambiguous verbs — use "Start export" not "Export" for CTA. ensure the signed download link includes rel="noopener" when opening. keyboard users should be able to toggle advanced options purely with keyboard; announce when job is queued ("Export queued. We'll notify you when ready.").

ben (PM): love the explicit copy. one more UX question: row selection in the preview — should export respect the UI filters & selection by default, or have a dropdown on the modal: "Export: [Selected rows | Filtered set | All]"?

sophia (Design): default to "Selected rows" if any selected, else "Filtered set". show the count next to the option. also micro-copy: "Selected rows (12)". keeps users from accidentally exporting everything.

eva (Research): also include a small "Estimated file size" near the modal footer that updates when format/sample changes. even rough estimates reduce confusion.

leo (Eng): we'll surface the estimate using sample * dims * bytes-per-value (float32 ~4 bytes). add a server-side fallback calculation for more accurate numbers.

ben (PM): next steps: sophia — update mock with the modal state (default selection behavior + advanced options collapsed). ana — quick accessibility checklist for the modal (focus, announcements, labels). leo — tech approach doc + API shape (include streaming vs job thresholds). eva — add sample + dedupe rationale for the help text. Can everyone thumbs up if this plan works? :thumbsup:

sophia (Design): 👍

leo (Eng): 👍

ana (Accessibility): 👍 (added a11y checklist items inline in figma comments)

eva (Research): 👍 — will add notes to the PR with user quotes.

ben (PM): thanks all. I'll file a ticket for the background job and link the mockups.
